title: Bermuda quarterly GDP
notes: Dates mark the end of each calendar year or quarter. Each row contains one observation. Missing observations are omitted, never replaced with zero.
Percentage values use the percent scale: 5 means 5%. Published growth is distinct from growth calculated from selected annual levels.
Values are snapshots of the supplied workbook’s cached results. Original workbooks retain formulas, revision history and full source references. Source workbook compilation date: 5 November 2026.
Real GDP at 2006 and 2013 prices is kept in separate series, including overlapping quarters; the two series are not spliced.
Nominal GDP combines release vintages. Published growth is retained from the selected release, not recalculated from the combined history.
All quarterly observations are provisional. The Q1 2026 release flags imports and related aggregates as not comparable with earlier releases; GDP includes these aggregates.
Coverage: 49 consecutive quarters, Q1 2014–Q1 2026, from all 45 reports linked on the official quarterly GDP page on 5 November 2026.
Measure and units: Total GDP by expenditure, in millions of Bermuda dollars. Quarterly amounts are not annualised and are not seasonally adjusted.

Real GDP bases: 2013-price real GDP is available from Q3 2018. The 2006-price series covers Q1 2014–Q2 2019. Their overlap is retained. The two level series have not been spliced, rescaled or backcast.

Nominal comparability: The latest current-price observations are retained for each quarter. Rebasing also revised nominal estimates and methods. Pre-Q3 2018 and later observations are not a uniformly revised historical vintage.

Growth rates: Both growth columns contain officially published changes from the same quarter a year earlier, divided by 100 for Excel percentage display. They are not calculated from mixed-vintage levels. Real growth uses the 2013-price source where available, otherwise 2006.

Recent warning: The Q1 2026 report warns that imports of goods and related aggregates are not comparable with earlier releases. GDP includes those aggregates. Treat comparisons between recent and older release vintages with caution.

Revisions: All data are provisional and subject to revision. Selection uses the latest printed publication month for each quarter, price basis and real base year. The later issue quarter breaks publication-month ties.

Audit: Published data retains all 450 total-GDP observations, including 348 superseded records. Selected marks 102 retained series-period observations, including four quarters where both real-price bases are retained. Source IDs identify publication vintages.

Provenance: Published data records source ID, printed month and PDF page for every value. Sources holds publication URLs. Publication months have month precision. Migrated URL folder dates do not establish publication chronology.
Missing levels: Empty real-GDP cells indicate that the linked releases did not provide that price-base estimate. They are not zero. No interpolation from annual GDP has been applied.

Supplied workbook: The supplied GDP workbook contains annual GDP by industry for 1996–2024. It is a different frequency and approach and was inspected for context. It was not used to manufacture quarterly estimates.

Extraction corrections: Q2 2021–Q4 2022 PDFs have damaged embedded-font text mappings. Total-GDP labels and numeric glyphs were decoded explicitly, with the original PDFs and extraction preserved. Printed month labels were visually checked.
Header correction: The Q3 2017 report labels its third column as 2016 Q1. The five-quarter sequence identifies it as 2017 Q1. That header correction is explicit in the extraction process.
description: GDP by expenditure, not seasonally adjusted or annualised. Nominal GDP, real GDP and published year-over-year growth.
